result.rationale: The diff verifiably adds an unconditional token refresh (fetch to login.salesforce.com plus prisma.credential.update) inside the SalesforceCalendarService connection setup, before returning the jsforce.Connection, with no expiry check on the existing access_token. This forces an extra network round-trip and a DB write on every instantiation, degrading connection creation; the mechanism described matches the code exactly. Whether maintainers intended the tradeoff is uncertain, but the unconditional behavior is a real regression risk introduced by this change.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the code now performs a refresh-token request and `prisma.credential.update(...)` unconditionally before returning `new jsforce.Connection(...)` (see the added `fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token"...)` block and subsequent DB update). There is no check for whether the existing `credential.key.access_token` is still valid/expired. This means every connection creation incurs an extra network round-trip and DB write, and if the refresh call fails it will throw/reject even though an existing access token might still be usable—matching the finding.
